Quick question as we finalize our security review: we need a written confirmation that production patient-facing model inferences for EU customers will be anchored to EU-hosted compute and storage. We also need clarity on telemetry/analytics — specifically if aggregated usage metrics or model telemetry (no raw patient text) may be processed outside the EU in a short failover/analytics window.

Two asks:
- A short note on the mechanics of your region-pinning (how you guarantee EU anchoring for request/response paths and storage).
- The maximum duration Redwood would allow transient processing outside EU for aggregated/telemetry-only flows and any monitoring/alerting tied to that window.

We have an internal timeline to sign by Sep 10 and would like to include a one-paragraph DPA addendum in our packet confirming the anchoring behavior and the short-window failover SLA. Can you loop in ops/legal?

Thanks — Alaine

Hi all,

Attached: subprocessor_roster_2027-09.csv and a first-pass DPA_Addendum_Anchoring_v1.1.pdf (redlines noted). High-level answers below which we can fold into a one-paragraph addendum for Orchid: 

- Region-pinning mechanism (plain language): inbound inference requests are routed to a regional gateway based on the customer account region (account metadata + IP/region preference). For EU-anchored customers, the request path, model execution (inference), and any full-response storage live on EU hosts. We use strict routing policies with a control-plane tag on the request (region=eu) that is enforced by the serving layer.

- Data classification split: PII/PHI inference input and model outputs are treated as "anchored data" and never leave the designated region for processing or storage except in the specific failover scenarios below. Aggregated telemetry (metrics, anonymized token counts, model-level quality metrics with no raw content) is eligible for cross-region processing for analytics.

- Failover/temporary processing windows: Our standard temporary failover window for analytics-only processing is 72 hours by default (for example, in a zone outage we may queue/ship aggregated telemetry to a nearby region for processing). For Orchid we can offer a tightened SLA to 48 hours max with additional monitoring/notification hooks. This would be documented in the DPA addendum.

- Monitoring / alerts: we can commit to alerting the customer within 2 hours of any event that triggers transient cross-region analytics processing, plus produce an incident report within 48 hours describing scope and duration.

- Evidence & runbook: ops-failover-runbook-snippet.txt (attached) includes the sequence: failover detection, non-PII data export path, encryption-in-transit, TTL for exports, and automated purge once EU capacity restored.

Next steps: legal (Neha) to review DPA wording; ops (Karthik) to review the technical descriptions and confirm we can commit to 48-hour window and 2-hour alerting in our SLA.

Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, alaine.peterson@orchidhealth.com

Subject: Re: Anchoring certification + short-window analytics processing

Marissa / Kimberly / Alaine — technical confirm below. I'm keeping the explanation concise for their one-paragraph addendum and attaching the ops snippet details.

- Enforcement: region tag is immutable for the request lifecycle. Serving nodes enforce location affinity; scheduler will not place inference containers outside of the pinned region unless an emergency failover policy is invoked.

- Temporary analytics path: aggregated telemetry is exported as batched, encrypted blobs. Export TTL: blobs are allowed temporary transit/processing outside EU only under declared failover (FAA) conditions. We enforce at-rest encryption and HMAC verifications on arrival.

- Duration control: we can implement an account-level max-transit TTL of 48 hours (instead of our default 72) for Orchid accounts. After TTL expiry, any remaining analytics data is auto-purged from non-EU processing nodes and we will provide purge confirmation.

- Operational telemetry & audit: we'll add an explicit audit field in the incident report showing which host/region processed telemetry, blob IDs, and purge timestamps. That will satisfy auditors.

- Limitations & edge cases: note that certain lower-level telemetry (kernel-level GPU crash dumps) may contain kernel metadata that is harder to fully anonymize; we isolate those and exclude them from cross-region exports by default, but if Orchid requires, we can add an explicit exclusion clause in the addendum.

I'll sign off on the 48-hour SLA if Legal is comfortable.

Thanks — Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
